app.title: BioT - Bioinformatics Tools
app.summary: A person loads a FASTA file of nucleotide or amino acid sequences, or picks a bundled example, and the file is checked and kept for the session. In the summary tool they pick one or more sequences and get, for each, its length, a table and bar chart of residue counts against an even expected share, the GC content, and a chi-square test of whether the composition is uniform. In the comparison tool they pick two nucleotide sequences and a window size and get a dotplot of every shared stretch, with a count of unique matches.

task.text: Describe the composition of sequences from a FASTA file and compare two nucleotide sequences for similar regions with a dotplot.

data.text: A FASTA file holding one or more nucleotide or amino acid sequences, each turned into a table of residue counts and frequencies.
data.item: one sequence record in a FASTA file

stage.text: exploring the sequences in a FASTA file, before alignment or deeper analysis

mechanism.text: A sidebar menu switches between tools while a sidebar loader holds one validated FASTA file that every tool reads; the summary tool repeats a collapsible report of numbers, a table and a bar chart for each selected sequence, and the comparison tool takes two picked sequences and a window size and draws matching windows as points on a scatter plot.

field.text: sequence composition statistics and dotplot comparison in bioinformatics

workflow.name: summarize the composition of sequences and compare two of them for shared regions

steps.here: Upload a FASTA file or choose a bundled example and press its upload button; the file is parsed as FASTA, rejected with an error if no records come out, and kept in the session with its name shown in the sidebar.

steps.step: choose which items to work on
steps.here: A multiselect lists the record names from the cached file; each chosen sequence opens its own collapsible report, in the order chosen.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For each sequence: record name, length, a table of residue counts with observed percent, expected percent if all residues were equally common and the difference, a bar chart of counts, and GC content.

steps.step: test whether the distribution departs from an expected one
steps.here: A chi-square goodness-of-fit test on the counts against a uniform distribution, reported with degrees of freedom, statistic and p, and a verdict on homogeneity at p = 0.05.

Pick a first and a second sequence and a window size (default 10, at least 5), press Generate dotplot; every window-length substring shared by both is plotted at its positions in each, with the count of unique matches above.

distinctive: Composition is judged against a uniform expectation with a chi-square test, so the person gets a yes/no verdict on whether a sequence's residues are evenly used.
The dotplot is built from exact matches of fixed-length windows, with the window size set by the person to trade noise for sensitivity.
The dotplot refuses sequences with anything other than A, C, G and T, while the summary accepts both nucleotide and amino acid sequences.
One validated file is cached for the whole session and shared by every tool until another is loaded.

parts.title: Main menu sidebar
parts.summary: Switches between the home page and the two tools, and holds the file loader and the name of the file currently cached.

parts.title: FASTA upload and example picker
parts.summary: Loads an uploaded FASTA file or a bundled example, validates that it parses into records, and caches it for the session.

DATA_EXAMPLES = [f for f in os.listdir('data') if f.endswith(('fasta', 'fa', 'txt'))]

parts.title: Sequence Summary tool
parts.summary: Lets the person pick one or more cached sequences and opens a collapsible composition report for each.

parts.title: Composition report
parts.summary: Shows a sequence's length, residue counts and frequencies against a uniform expectation as a table and bar chart, its GC content, and a chi-square test of homogeneity.

parts.title: Two Sequence Alignment tool
parts.summary: Takes two chosen sequences and a window size, checks both are nucleotide sequences, and asks for a dotplot.

parts.title: Dotplot
parts.summary: Finds every window-length substring shared by the two sequences and plots each pair of positions as a point, with the number of unique matches.
